title: FAST Studio API
intro: Everything the FAST Studio screens can do is also an HTTP API. This page explains each feature's endpoints in plain words and gives a ready curl for every one. Fill in your values once at the top (server address, token, IDs): every example on the page updates. Paste a curl into a terminal, or import it into Postman (Import → Raw text), or download the whole Postman collection.
auth: Most endpoints need a token in the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Easiest for scripts, Postman and AI assistants: a **personal access token** (`fsp_…`). Make one on your profile (Profile and Settings → API Tokens) and paste it into the Token box above. It works only for the organization and role you chose, until it expires or you revoke it.
Alternatively sign in with email and password (`POST /api/auth/token`, below) and use the `access_token` from the answer; it lasts 10 minutes and the `refresh_token` gets a new one.

Project endpoints take the organization in the path: `/api/orgs/{org}/…`, where `{org}` is the project's short name (e.g. `aurora`) or its ID. You must be a member, and your token must be for that organization; otherwise the answer is 404.
Platform endpoints (`/api/platform/…`) are for platform administrators only and use IDs (UUIDs) for organizations and tenants.

Errors come back as JSON with a `code` and a plain `detail` message, for example 400 (invalid input), 403 (not allowed), 404 (not found or not yours), 409 (conflict, e.g. someone changed the schedule), 429 (too many requests).

categories.title: Sign-in and tokens
categories.summary: Getting a token, refreshing it, switching project, signing out, and managing your personal access tokens.
categories.who: Anyone with an account. Sign-in endpoints need no token.

endpoints.title: Sign in (get a token)
endpoints.description: Email and password in, a 10-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token out. For scripts and partner systems; the browser uses /api/auth/login instead. Too many wrong passwords are slowed down (429).

endpoints.title: Refresh the access token
endpoints.description: Gives a new access token and a new refresh token. The old refresh token stops working; reusing it signs out that sign-in everywhere (it was stolen).

endpoints.title: Switch project
endpoints.description: A new access token for another organization you belong to. Personal access tokens can't switch: they are fixed to one organization.

endpoints.title: Who am I
endpoints.description: The signed-in person, the active organization with its role and permissions, and the organizations you can switch to.

endpoints.title: Browser sign-in
endpoints.description: The screen's sign-in: puts the tokens in secure cookies instead of the answer. Scripts should use Sign in (get a token).

endpoints.title: Sign out
endpoints.description: Ends this sign-in (its refresh token). Always answers 204.

endpoints.title: Sign out everywhere
endpoints.description: Ends every sign-in of yours on every device; access tokens stop working at once.

endpoints.title: Change password
endpoints.description: Needs the current password. Signs out other sign-ins.

endpoints.title: Forgot password
endpoints.description: Emails a reset link if the address has an account. Always answers the same, so nobody can find out who has an account.

endpoints.title: Reset password with the emailed code
endpoints.description: The token comes from the reset email link.

endpoints.title: Sign-in options
endpoints.description: What the sign-in screen offers on this server (for example whether demo accounts are shown).

endpoints.title: Demo accounts
endpoints.description: The fictional demo people (demo mode only; empty in a pilot).

endpoints.title: CSRF token (browsers only)
endpoints.description: Browsers using cookies need this value in an X-XSRF-TOKEN header for changes. Calls with a Bearer token don't.

endpoints.title: List my personal access tokens
endpoints.description: Your active tokens: name, organization, role, last used and expiry. The secret itself is never shown again.

endpoints.title: Create a personal access token
endpoints.description: Shown once in the answer (field token). org is a project short name or ID, or "platform" for platform administrators. role can't be higher than yours. expiresInDays: 1–3650, or leave it out for no expiry. Can't be called with a personal access token itself.

endpoints.title: Revoke a personal access token
endpoints.description: Stops it at once. The id comes from List my personal access tokens.

endpoints.title: Public signing keys
endpoints.description: Lets other systems verify FAST Studio access tokens (ES256) without calling us.

categories.title: Project, settings and team
categories.summary: What the project is, its programming and media settings, configuration values, and who works in it.
categories.who: Members of the project. Changing settings and the team needs an owner or admin.

endpoints.title: Project details
endpoints.description: The project's identity (ID, name, tenant), your role and permissions, enabled features and limits. A good first call: it also tells you the organization ID.

endpoints.title: Dashboard
endpoints.description: The home screen numbers: channels on air, videos, upcoming schedule coverage, open alerts.

endpoints.title: Media and programming settings
endpoints.description: Enabled media types, default type, default premiere time and weekdays, personalized ads, and a revision number to send back when saving.

endpoints.title: Save media and programming settings
endpoints.description: Send expectedRevision from the settings you read; if someone saved in between you get 409 and should reload.

endpoints.title: Set the viewer-context signing key
endpoints.description: Write-only key (32+ characters) your apps use to sign viewer context for personalized ads. Never returned.

endpoints.title: Project configuration
endpoints.description: Connectors and properties as they apply to this project (global default → tenant → project override).

endpoints.title: Override a property for this project
endpoints.description: Send {"reset": true} instead to go back to the inherited value.

endpoints.title: Switch a connector on or off for this project
endpoints.description: Only connectors the platform made available to your tenant. Switching off keeps existing media and credentials.

endpoints.title: Tenant-wide settings
endpoints.description: Settings shared by all projects of your company (owners and admins).

endpoints.title: Set a tenant-wide property
endpoints.description: Applies to every project of the tenant that doesn't override it.

endpoints.title: List members
endpoints.description: People in the project with their roles.

endpoints.title: Roles you can give
endpoints.description: Built-in and custom roles, limited to those not higher than yours.

endpoints.title: Invite a member
endpoints.description: Adds the person (creating the account if needed and emailing a temporary password). Roles: OWNER, ADMIN, CONTENT_MANAGER, CHANNEL_OPERATOR, AD_OPS, ANALYST.

endpoints.title: Change a member's role
endpoints.description: You can't give a role higher than your own; only owners manage owners.

endpoints.title: Remove a member
endpoints.description: The project always keeps at least one owner; you can't remove yourself.

endpoints.title: Send a member a password reset
endpoints.description: Emails them a reset link.

endpoints.title: Activity log
endpoints.description: Who did what in the project, newest first.

endpoints.title: Project features and permissions
endpoints.description: The catalogue this project can use (global entries plus its own), and the feature and permission identifiers that apply to you now. The same keys are in project details (access.features, access.permissions).

fields.kind: FEATURE (switched on per project) or PERMISSION (given to people through roles).
fields.category: Group shown on screens, e.g. Media or Advertising (default General).
fields.enabled: true = in use, false = switched off. Built-in entries can't be switched off.

endpoints.description: Changes one of this project's own entries (404 for global entries or another project's). Needs TEAM_MANAGE.

categories.title: Video library
categories.summary: Videos (assets): list, create, upload, edit metadata and cue points, retry, archive, and sync from the connected video library.
categories.who: Content managers, admins and owners change videos; every member can read.

endpoints.title: List videos
endpoints.description: All videos with status, signed thumbnail/preview links, rights status and where they air. Filter with q (text), kind (MOVIE, EPISODE, SHORT, AD) or archived=true.

endpoints.title: One video
endpoints.description: The same fields as the list, for one video.

endpoints.title: Create a video
endpoints.description: Creates the entry (status DRAFT) waiting for a file. With sampleSeconds the server generates a fictional demo clip instead (needs ffmpeg). Episodes need series, season and episode, unique in the project.

endpoints.title: Upload the video file
endpoints.description: Multipart upload (field file): MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, M4V. The server converts it into 5-second segments in three qualities; status goes PROCESSING → READY. Limited by the project's stored hours and conversions at once (409).

endpoints.title: Get a direct-upload address
endpoints.description: A one-time https address to PUT the file to directly (connected video library). The file never passes through our server; when the library has it, conversion starts by itself.

endpoints.title: Edit metadata and cue points
endpoints.description: Only the fields you send change. cuePoints are milliseconds; they snap to 5-second boundaries.

endpoints.title: Retry a failed conversion
endpoints.description: Only for videos with status FAILED.

endpoints.title: Processing history of a video
endpoints.description: The last 10 background jobs of the video, newest first: state (QUEUED, RUNNING, CANCEL_REQUESTED, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED), lane (AD or PROGRAMME), attempt number out of the maximum, the last error in plain words and times. nextRunAt is set while a job waits for its retry.

endpoints.title: Cancel processing
endpoints.description: Stops the video's processing. A queued job is cancelled at once; a running one stops within about 30 seconds. The video goes back to how it was: still READY with its old media (which keeps airing), or DRAFT if it never had media. 409 NOT_PROCESSING when nothing is queued or running.

endpoints.title: Archive a video
endpoints.description: Hides it from the library (never a hard delete). Refused while it airs, is in a draft, is a channel's fallback or an active campaign's creative; the answer lists where.

endpoints.title: Connected library status
endpoints.description: Whether a video library is connected and its last check worked, what it can do (CATALOGUE: sync, DIRECT_UPLOAD: upload URLs, SOURCE_FILE: prepare for broadcast, WEBHOOKS: automatic updates) and the sync: state (NEVER, QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED), videos seen, videos added, pages read, whether the last full scan completed, the last error and when a waiting sync retries. Never names the provider.

endpoints.title: Start a library sync
endpoints.description: Starts reading the connected library in the background, page by page, and adds every ready video not imported yet as a Draft (catalogue only: nothing is prepared or paid for). If the library is unreachable the sync waits and continues from the last saved page. A second call while one runs just reports it. The answer is the sync status (see GET …/library). Needs asset editing and the library-sync feature.

endpoints.title: Prepare library videos for broadcast
endpoints.description: Queues the chosen library videos (1 to 100) for conversion into 5-second segments, which fetches their original files from the library. Each video is checked on its own; the answer says how many were queued and, for the others, why not: NOT_FOUND, NOT_FROM_LIBRARY, ALREADY_READY, ALREADY_PROCESSING, NOT_READY_IN_LIBRARY (the library reports it errored, deleted or missing) or PROCESSING_LIMIT. 409 NOT_SUPPORTED when the connected library can't hand over files. Needs asset editing.

categories.title: Rights and availability
categories.summary: Where and when each video may be shown, and checking a country and time before scheduling.
categories.who: Content managers, admins and owners set rights; members can check.

endpoints.title: Set a video's rights
endpoints.description: Allowed and blocked countries (2-letter codes, WW = worldwide), licence window and whether ads may run. Blank allowed countries means incomplete rights, never worldwide.

endpoints.title: Can it play there and then?
endpoints.description: Checks one video for a country and time (optionally on a channel). The country is your input, not a location lookup.

categories.title: Channels
categories.summary: 24/7 linear channels: create, edit, go live, stop, archive.
categories.who: Channel operators, admins and owners change channels; every member can read.

endpoints.title: List channels
endpoints.description: Every channel with what is on now and next, its published version and how far ahead it is scheduled.

endpoints.title: One channel
endpoints.description: The same as the list, for one channel, including readiness to go live.

endpoints.title: Create a channel
endpoints.description: Name and territories are the essentials. Optionally pass assetIds and autofillHours to start with a filled schedule. Limited by your plan's channel allowance.

endpoints.title: Edit a channel
endpoints.description: Only the fields you send change. clearFallback: true removes the fallback video.

endpoints.title: Go live
endpoints.description: Starts streaming the published schedule. Refused until the channel is ready (published schedule, ready videos).

endpoints.title: Stop streaming
endpoints.description: Takes the channel off air; viewers see the standby slate.

endpoints.title: Archive a channel
endpoints.description: Stops and hides the channel. Kept for reports; never hard-deleted.

categories.title: Schedule and EPG
categories.summary: The draft schedule of a channel, publishing it, versions, and the programme guide (EPG) partners read.
categories.who: Channel operators, admins and owners edit and publish; every member can read.

endpoints.title: Read the schedule
endpoints.description: Draft and published entries from now (or from=ISO time) for the given hours, plus problems found and the draft's revision number (send it back as expectedRevision when editing).

endpoints.title: Add a programme or break
endpoints.description: kind PROGRAM with an assetId (and withBreaks to insert ad breaks at its cue points) or AD_BREAK with seconds. startAt omitted = after the last entry. Times snap to 5 seconds.

endpoints.title: Remove an entry
endpoints.description: wholeProgramme=true also removes the programme's ad breaks and other parts.

endpoints.title: Fill the schedule automatically
endpoints.description: Fills the next hours with ready videos (all, or the assetIds you pass), with ad breaks. replace: true starts from empty.

endpoints.title: Close gaps
endpoints.description: Moves later entries up so there is no dead air between programmes.

endpoints.title: Clear the draft
endpoints.description: Empties the future part of the draft. The published schedule is unchanged until you publish.

endpoints.title: Publish
endpoints.description: Makes the draft the live schedule as a new version. Refused (422) with the list of problems if it has errors (rights, missing videos, overlaps).

endpoints.title: Restore an older version into the draft
endpoints.description: Copies published version N into the draft; publish to make it live again.

endpoints.title: Programme guide (JSON)
endpoints.description: The published schedule as viewers see it: titles, times, descriptions.

endpoints.title: Programme guide (XMLTV)
endpoints.description: The same guide in XMLTV format, which TV platforms import.

endpoints.title: Ad break inventory
endpoints.description: Upcoming ad breaks with their length and checks (markers, rights) for ad sales.

categories.title: Smart programming
categories.summary: Rules that schedule a series by themselves: premiere a new episode on chosen weekdays, repeats, season roll-over and loops.

endpoints.title: List rules
endpoints.description: The channel's series rules and what they planned.

endpoints.title: Preview a rule
endpoints.description: Shows which episodes would air when, without saving anything.

endpoints.title: Create a rule
endpoints.description: Saves the rule; generate then writes its episodes into the draft schedule.

endpoints.title: Pause or resume a rule
endpoints.description: enabled: false stops it from generating further.

endpoints.title: Generate into the draft
endpoints.description: Writes the next days (1–31) of all active rules into the draft. It never publishes by itself.

categories.title: Advertising
categories.summary: Direct-sold campaigns, ad servers (VAST), testing ad tags and simulating an ad break.

endpoints.title: List campaigns
endpoints.description: Campaigns with dates, targeting, priority, CPM and delivery so far (estimates in the demo).

endpoints.title: Create a campaign
endpoints.description: creativeAssetId is a ready video of kind AD. Territories and audiences narrow where it runs; frequencyCap limits views per viewer per day.

endpoints.title: Edit a campaign
endpoints.description: Send the whole campaign again.

endpoints.title: Pause, resume or end a campaign
endpoints.description: status: ACTIVE, PAUSED or ENDED.

endpoints.title: List ad servers
endpoints.description: The ad sources tried in order for each break (direct campaigns, VAST ad servers). Tag addresses are never shown. Needs the ad-server connector switched on for your project by the platform; otherwise 403 FEATURE_OFF (the demo project has it off).

endpoints.title: Add an ad server
endpoints.description: kind VAST with a public https tagUrl, or DIRECT. The tag address is stored encrypted.

fields.kind: VAST (an ad server tag) or DIRECT (your campaigns).

endpoints.title: Edit an ad server
endpoints.description: Leave tagUrl out to keep the stored one.

fields.kind: VAST (an ad server tag) or DIRECT (your campaigns).

endpoints.title: Remove an ad server
endpoints.description: Removes it from the waterfall.

endpoints.title: Test an ad tag
endpoints.description: Calls the tag once and shows what came back (ads, wrappers, errors). prepare: true also converts the returned creatives so they can air.

endpoints.title: Simulate an ad break
endpoints.description: Which ads a viewer in a country would get in the channel's next break, and why.

categories.title: Distribution and partners
categories.summary: Where channels are delivered (destinations), publishing to them, and sharing channels with partner TV platforms.
categories.who: Channel operators, admins and owners (sharing: owners and admins).

endpoints.title: List destinations
endpoints.description: Your web player and partner TV platforms, with ad mode and marker format.

endpoints.title: Add a destination
endpoints.description: adMode SSAI (ads stitched in), SGAI (player inserts) or PASSTHROUGH; markerFormat DATERANGE or CUE_OUT.

endpoints.title: Publish a channel to a destination
endpoints.description: Runs the delivery checks (live, 6 hours scheduled, EPG, ad load, markers) and records the result. Partner deliveries are simulated in this prototype.

endpoints.title: List partner shares
endpoints.description: Which partners see which channels and what they may read.

endpoints.title: Partner directory
endpoints.description: Partner organizations you can share with.

endpoints.title: Share channels with a partner
endpoints.description: Scopes: channels:read, epg:read, stream:read, breaks:read, delivery:read. allChannels: true includes future channels. The partner admins get an email to accept.

endpoints.title: Change a share
endpoints.description: New channels or scopes for an existing share.

endpoints.title: Stop sharing
endpoints.description: The partner loses access at once.

categories.title: Monitoring and analytics
categories.summary: Alerts about channels and content, and viewing and ad numbers.
categories.who: Every member reads; channel operators and ad operations handle alerts.

endpoints.title: List alerts
endpoints.description: Problems found automatically (channel off air, schedule running out, failed videos, expiring rights) and their state.

endpoints.title: Check now
endpoints.description: Runs the checks immediately instead of waiting for the next minute.

endpoints.title: Acknowledge an alert
endpoints.description: Marks it as seen by you.

endpoints.title: Resolve an alert
endpoints.description: Closes it with a note on what was done.

endpoints.title: Analytics
endpoints.description: Sessions, ad impressions, completion, ad seconds and estimated revenue per channel and campaign (demo numbers are not revenue).

categories.title: Partner API (for TV platforms)
categories.summary: What a partner organization reads from the customers that share with it, and its machine credentials.
categories.who: Members of a partner organization, or its API clients (client-credentials tokens).

endpoints.title: Machine token (client credentials)
endpoints.description: An API client of the partner exchanges its id and secret (HTTP Basic) for a 10-minute token, usable only on /api/partners/…. Make a client with Create an API client first.

endpoints.title: Shares received
endpoints.description: Which customers share which channels with this partner, and whether the share was accepted.

endpoints.title: Accept a share
endpoints.description: A partner admin accepts; reading starts working after that.

endpoints.title: Shared channels
endpoints.description: The channels this customer shares with you (needs channels:read).

endpoints.title: One shared channel
endpoints.description: Name, genre, language, territories, live or not.

endpoints.title: Guide (JSON)
endpoints.description: The programme guide (needs epg:read).

endpoints.title: Guide (XMLTV)
endpoints.description: The guide in XMLTV for import into your platform.

endpoints.title: Stream address
endpoints.description: Where to play the channel and the ad and marker settings for your destination (needs stream:read).

endpoints.title: Ad breaks ahead
endpoints.description: Upcoming ad breaks with their times and SCTE-35 markers (needs breaks:read).

endpoints.title: Delivery report
endpoints.description: Sessions and ads delivered on your platform (needs delivery:read). Without that scope in the share the answer is 404, as for anything not shared (the demo share doesn't include it).

endpoints.title: List API clients
endpoints.description: The partner's machine credentials (secrets never shown again).

endpoints.title: Create an API client
endpoints.description: Answers once with clientId and clientSecret for /oauth/token. Partner admins only.

endpoints.title: Revoke an API client
endpoints.description: Its tokens stop working within seconds.

categories.title: Playback (viewers and players)
categories.summary: Starting a viewing session for a live channel, ad decisions and beacons, and signed media files. Used by players; no sign-in.
categories.who: Public: anyone who can reach the channel. Everything is bound to the session's channel.

endpoints.title: Start a viewing session
endpoints.description: org and channel are short names; country is where the viewer is (2 letters). The answer has sessionId and playlistUrl: open that in any HLS player. A destinationId chooses ad mode; viewerToken carries signed viewer context for personalized ads.

endpoints.title: Session info
endpoints.description: What is on now and next for this session, and whether it may play in the viewer's country.

endpoints.title: Ads for a break
endpoints.description: Which ads fill this break for this viewer (SGAI players ask this; with SSAI the stream already contains them).

endpoints.title: Report ad progress
endpoints.description: event: IMPRESSION, FIRST_QUARTILE, MIDPOINT, THIRD_QUARTILE, COMPLETE. Each is counted once.

endpoints.title: Viewer opts out of personalized ads
endpoints.description: From now on this session only gets contextual (not personalized) ads.

endpoints.title: Signed media files
endpoints.description: Thumbnails, previews and segments are served only from signed, expiring addresses that the other endpoints return (for example thumbUrl in List videos). They can't be made by hand.

categories.title: Tools and webhooks
categories.summary: Helpers for broadcast engineers, and inbound webhooks from the video library.
categories.who: Tools: any signed-in member. Webhooks: the video library, verified by signature.

endpoints.title: SCTE-35 example
endpoints.description: An example ad-break marker (base64 and hex) to try the decoder with.

endpoints.title: Decode an SCTE-35 marker
endpoints.description: Paste a marker as base64 or hex: the answer explains every field in plain words.

endpoints.title: Video library webhook (Mux)
endpoints.description: Set this address in the library's webhook settings (Platform → Connectors shows it). Each delivery must carry a valid Mux-Signature made with the project's webhook secret, otherwise 401; unknown project 404. Replays are harmless.

categories.title: Platform: tenants, projects and plans
categories.summary: Customer accounts (tenants), their projects, subscriptions, configuration, limits, export and deletion.
categories.who: Platform administrators only (a platform personal access token works).

endpoints.title: List tenants
endpoints.description: Every customer tenant with status, plan, projects and channel counts. Gives the tenant IDs used below.

endpoints.title: Suspend or reactivate a tenant
endpoints.description: SUSPENDED blocks management in all its projects (channels keep streaming); ACTIVE restores it.

fields.status: SUSPENDED blocks management; ACTIVE restores it.

endpoints.title: Change plan and subscription status
endpoints.description: Send expectedRevision from List tenants.

endpoints.title: Possible project owners
endpoints.description: Existing owners and admins of the tenant, to choose as owner of a new project.

endpoints.title: Add a project
endpoints.description: Within the plan's project allowance; ownerUserId from Possible project owners.

endpoints.title: Tenant configuration
endpoints.description: Connectors and properties as set for the tenant (global default → tenant).

endpoints.title: Project configuration
endpoints.description: The same for one project, including its overrides.

endpoints.title: Set a tenant property or limit
endpoints.description: Limits: limits.api_requests_per_minute, limits.media_hours, limits.processing_videos (whole numbers, 0 = unlimited). {"reset": true} returns to the global default.

endpoints.title: Set a property or limit for one project
endpoints.description: Overrides the tenant value for this project only.

endpoints.title: Make a connector available to a tenant
endpoints.description: enabled true/false, or reset to inherit.

endpoints.title: Connector for one project
endpoints.description: Overrides the tenant setting for this project.

endpoints.title: Export all tenant data
endpoints.description: Everything the tenant owns as one JSON file (projects, members, every table's rows), without credentials or video files. Recorded in the audit log.

endpoints.description: Only while suspended, and only with the tenant's exact name. Removes all its projects and data, takes its channels off the air and anonymizes people who belonged only to it. Cannot be undone: export first.

fields.confirm: The tenant's exact name, to prove you mean it.

endpoints.title: List plans
endpoints.description: Subscription plans with allowances and features.

endpoints.title: Create or update a plan
endpoints.description: Allowances apply across a whole tenant.

endpoints.title: List properties
endpoints.description: Every configurable property with its type, default and whether projects may override it.

endpoints.title: Create or update a property
endpoints.description: Custom settings for tenants and projects. Secret values are stored encrypted and never returned.

endpoints.title: Clear a property's default
endpoints.description: Removes the global default value.

endpoints.title: List connectors
endpoints.description: Connector types the platform offers (video library, ad servers, storage).

endpoints.title: Create or update a connector
endpoints.description: The driver chooses the server adapter and can't change later.

endpoints.title: List custom roles
endpoints.description: Roles beyond the built-in ones, with their permissions.

endpoints.title: Create or update a custom role
endpoints.description: Based on a built-in role, with a chosen permission set.

fields.kind: CUSTOMER or PARTNER: where the role can be used.

endpoints.title: Features and permissions catalogue
endpoints.description: Every global feature and permission: identifier, kind (FEATURE or PERMISSION), name, description, category, whether it is built in (enforced by the server) and whether it is switched on. Platform administrators only.

endpoints.title: Add a global feature or permission

fields.key: Identifier screens check: capitals, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (e.g. CLIPS_EXPORT). Unique across the platform; it can't change later.
fields.kind: FEATURE (switched on per project) or PERMISSION (given to people through roles).
fields.category: Group shown on screens, e.g. Media or Advertising (default General).
fields.enabled: true = in use, false = switched off. Built-in entries can't be switched off.

endpoints.description: Adds an entry every project can use. A feature is then switched on per project (PUT /api/platform/orgs/{orgId}/features); a permission goes to owners and administrators and to custom roles that list it. Added entries are identifiers for screens; they grant no server access by themselves. 409 KEY_TAKEN if the identifier exists anywhere.

endpoints.title: Change a global feature or permission

fields.key: Identifier screens check: capitals, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (e.g. CLIPS_EXPORT). Unique across the platform; it can't change later.
fields.kind: FEATURE (switched on per project) or PERMISSION (given to people through roles).
fields.category: Group shown on screens, e.g. Media or Advertising (default General).
fields.enabled: true = in use, false = switched off. Built-in entries can't be switched off.

endpoints.description: Renames, re-describes or switches an entry on or off. The identifier and kind never change. Built-in entries can be renamed but not switched off (409 BUILT_IN).

endpoints.title: Remove a global feature or permission
endpoints.description: Removes an added entry. Built-in entries can't be removed (409 BUILT_IN). Projects that had the feature switched on simply stop seeing it.

categories.title: Platform: organizations, connectors and media types
categories.summary: Organizations (customer projects and partners), their video library and ad server connections, features and media types, password help.

endpoints.title: List organizations
endpoints.description: Every organization with counts only (no content or money). Gives the organization IDs used below.

endpoints.title: Create an organization
endpoints.description: A customer (new tenant with its first project) or a partner, with its first owner who gets an email.

fields.kind: CUSTOMER (a new tenant with its first project) or PARTNER.

endpoints.title: Suspend or reactivate an organization
endpoints.description: SUSPENDED or ACTIVE.

endpoints.title: Project details (platform view)
endpoints.description: The same project details a member sees, for support.

endpoints.title: Set a project's features
endpoints.description: Within its plan, e.g. LIBRARY_SYNC.

endpoints.title: A project's connectors
endpoints.description: Video library and ad servers of the project and their state.

endpoints.title: Video library account (Mux)
endpoints.description: Whether it is connected, its environment and tag, the webhook address to enter in Mux, and the last connection check (healthy null = never checked). Never the credentials.

endpoints.title: Connect the video library (Mux)
endpoints.description: Credentials are stored encrypted and never returned. Leave token fields blank to keep the stored ones. passthroughTag: only videos with this tag are imported.

endpoints.title: Check the video library connection
endpoints.description: Reads the library with the stored credentials and records the result: healthy true, or false with checkError in plain words. Saving credentials alone never marks a connection as working; new credentials clear the last result.

endpoints.title: A project's library sync status
endpoints.description: State of the latest sync (NEVER, QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED), videos seen and added, pages read, whether the full scan completed, the last error and when a waiting sync retries.

endpoints.title: Start a project's library sync
endpoints.description: Starts the same background sync as the project's own sync button: new ready videos are added as Drafts, nothing is prepared. The answer is the sync status.

endpoints.title: A project's ad servers
endpoints.description: The ad waterfall as the platform manages it.

endpoints.title: Add an ad server for a project
endpoints.description: As the project endpoint, managed by the platform.

fields.kind: VAST (an ad server tag) or DIRECT (your campaigns).

endpoints.title: Edit a project's ad server
endpoints.description: Leave tagUrl out to keep it.

fields.kind: VAST (an ad server tag) or DIRECT (your campaigns).

endpoints.title: Remove a project's ad server
endpoints.description: Removes it from the waterfall.

endpoints.title: Reorder the waterfall
endpoints.description: The ids in the order to try them.

endpoints.title: Test an ad tag for a project
endpoints.description: As the project endpoint.

endpoints.title: List media types
endpoints.description: Platform-wide media types (MOVIE, EPISODE, … and custom ones) and their scheduling behaviour.

endpoints.title: Create or update a media type
endpoints.description: kind decides how it schedules: MOVIE, EPISODE, SHORT or AD.

fields.key: Upper-case key, e.g. CONCERT (letters, digits, underscore).
fields.kind: How it schedules: MOVIE, EPISODE, SHORT or AD.

endpoints.title: A project's media types
endpoints.description: Which media types the project may use.

endpoints.title: Set a project's media types
endpoints.description: The full list of types it may use.

endpoints.title: Send someone a password reset
endpoints.description: For support: emails the person a reset link.

categories.title: Platform: email
categories.summary: Email templates, the sent-mail log and test emails.

endpoints.title: Email status
endpoints.description: Whether mail is really sent (SMTP) or only saved to the outbox folder, and from which address.

endpoints.title: Sent mail log
endpoints.description: Recent emails with status. One-time passwords and links are hidden in the log.

endpoints.title: One email
endpoints.description: Subject and body as logged (secrets hidden).

endpoints.title: Resend a failed email
endpoints.description: Only failed emails that still have their text.

endpoints.title: List templates
endpoints.description: Every email the system sends, with the placeholders it may use.

endpoints.title: Customise a template
endpoints.description: Placeholders like {{name}} are filled in when sent.

body.subject: Welcome to {{orgName}}, {{name}}
body.body:
Hello {{name}},

You have been invited to {{orgName}}.

endpoints.title: Preview a template
endpoints.description: Renders it with sample values, without sending.

endpoints.title: Back to the built-in template
endpoints.description: Removes your customisation.

endpoints.title: Send a test email
endpoints.description: Checks that mail delivery works.
